why: Round 86 announces 'The three of the other shift are coming up' and 'You have a round, maybe two.' Round 87 turns three into a dozen.

quote: Dreg walked the road beside you for three days.
why: Korvash was marched from the children's road (Day 19, 1:45 PM) to Greyshaft (Day 20, ~6 PM), under two days. Also round 63 had called it a three-day road and round 64 a night's march.

quote: my rider goes to the Border Stones
why: In round 82 the Foreman wrote and sealed an order for his rider to turn back from the Border Stones ('Done before you speak'). In round 90 the rider is again a threat still to be sent, with no explanation.

quote: you swing your chained fists across the desk. The lantern bursts
why: Round 96 puts Korvash on the floor and then at the barred door, and has the Foreman walking to the barred door too ('He doesn't touch it'), with the lantern on his desk. Round 97 has Korvash smash that lantern from the door and set the Foreman's sleeve alight, with no movement between.

quote: Behind you, forty hobgoblin spears stop walking.
why: Round 115 says Brakk and nine Tally-sworn deserted the column on Day 22 night, and Gorrak knew by morning. The column should be about thirty spears. Rounds 104, 106 and 107 still say forty.

quote: She has been to the Goat's Throat on a dozen nights alone
why: In the same reply Tessa says 'I've not seen it since.' Round 110 has her carrying the stone since age seven out of fear of putting it back, and round 111 'I've not been here in years'.

quote: You untie the white goat from the cairn rope
why: In round 110 the goat was tied to the cairn and in round 111 it was walked to the ledge and slept there. The player's round 112 text is untie it 'under the seep'; the cairn rope no longer fits.

quote: And I found the ledge, three days after. A child's tally on the wall.
why: Round 111 has eleven tally marks in the ledge, 'Eleven nights', which implies the children stayed there that long. Ushk says he found the ledge three days after, saw the tally and swept the empty floor. Either the children were gone by day three or they were found.

quote: He left the column the second night, at the Hollin spring.
why: The column left Greyshaft on Day 22 and camped at Hollin Cairn Camp that night, which was the first night on the road. The notebook gives 'the night of Day 22'.

Hale Orrin was asked to lend ponies and agreed ('Four ponies and a mule'). The pony is not stolen. The reply also has the ponies stamping 'at the Stones' while Pip stands 'by Veshra's gate' watching the party leave.

quote: His eyes have begun to flutter.
why: R123 (8 AM) has Brakk starting to wake, but R124 says "Brakk wakes at dusk on the first night", about ten hours later, with nothing explaining the gap.

quote: The cloak beside him catches the worst of the rest and goes down in a heap, smoking.
why: R142 has this cloak (Cloak 3) down in a heap. In R143 he is up, with 1 HP, firing a crossbow at Korvash, which is not what "down" in R142 implied.

quote: Cloak 8 crossbow vs unconscious Korvash (advantage; not within 5 ft, so no auto-crit)
why: Cloak 8 is one of the three cloaks who dropped their bows and sat apart (R139 morale, R140 "the three who dropped them", R142 "not looking at you at all"), yet here he fires at Korvash.

quote: I can't build a new character sheet here. My tools only add companions to an existing party
why: In R144 the DM offered "I can start a new character in Harrowmere". One round later it says it cannot create one, so the offer was empty.

quote: When the roar came down the pass, he turned and went east, fast. Toward Greyshaft.
why: Greyshaft is to the north: R135 says the tracks come "from the north along the old herd track, the Greyshaft side". The rider flees east "toward Greyshaft".

quote: Tolk," he says at last, hoarse. "Deputy to the Foreman. He has the lower galleries and the second ledger and about twenty cloaks.
why: In R140 Skarn says "now I am the senior one left" in the Foreman's house. Here a senior deputy with twenty cloaks and a ledger exists, and Skarn knew all along.

quote: your arms ache from holding the shield
why: The player said the shield was "propped against my knee", and the DM's own R163 narration says the same, so she is not holding it.

quote: Four crossbows hit the frost, then three more
why: The tracker removes four cloaks (11, 13, 15, 16) on the surrender call. The story says four plus three, then "Seven more throw down their bows", which would be 14 of 16 surrendering instead of the 11 the tracker shows.

quote: Tolk twists behind the iron of his own shield
why: R135 and R136 describe the grey cloaks as "crossbows and short swords, no shields". Yet their AC is 18 and Tolk (and Skarn in R139) have shields and longswords.
